questions.question: A woman in her 60s presents with 4 months of progressive proximal muscle weakness, dysphagia, dysphonia, and CK elevation to ~4000 U/L. What diagnoses should be considered, and what key elements of the history, examination, and laboratory workup would help narrow the differential?

What are the characteristic histopathological findings on muscle biopsy that distinguish immune-mediated necrotising myopathy (IMNM) from polymyositis, and what does the presence of membrane attack complex (MAC/C5b-9) deposition on non-necrotic muscle fibers suggest about the pathogenic mechanism?

Which two myositis-specific autoantibodies are most strongly associated with IMNM? What medication class is a well-known trigger for one of these antibody-associated forms, and approximately what proportion of IMNM patients are seronegative for both?

In a patient who develops muscle weakness and CK elevation after exposure to a medication, what clinical and laboratory features distinguish drug-induced immune-mediated necrotising myopathy from direct toxic rhabdomyolysis, and how does the CK trajectory differ between the two conditions?

What is the standard treatment approach for IMNM, and how might the treatment course differ between drug-induced IMNM (after withdrawal of the offending agent) and idiopathic IMNM in terms of intensity and duration of immunosuppression?

What adverse effects on skeletal muscle have been described with GLP-1 receptor agonists? How does the clinical course of the previously reported tirzepatide-associated rhabdomyolysis case differ from the semaglutide-associated IMNM described in this report?

A patient with known hepatic steatosis and an inflammatory myopathy has elevated transaminases (AST and ALT) and a mildly elevated high-sensitivity troponin. How would you determine whether these abnormalities are due to the myopathy itself versus hepatic and cardiac disease, and what additional testing might help clarify the source?

According to the WHO-Uppsala Monitoring Centre causality assessment criteria, what factors in this case support 'probable' (as opposed to 'possible' or 'certain') causality between semaglutide and IMNM, and why was rechallenge not performed?
